prompt: Predict insurance claims from 60 tabular columns mixing numbers and categories. Accuracy matters most.
tells: 60 tabular columns mixing numbers and categories
why: Boosted trees handle mixed types, missing values and interactions, and usually win on tabular data.
trap: Deep nets rarely beat boosted trees on ordinary tables.

prompt: Churn depends on combinations, like low usage only matters for customers on annual plans. A linear model misses this.
why: Trees capture interactions automatically without you engineering them.
trap: You could hand-craft interaction terms, but trees find them for you.

prompt: You have millions of labeled transactions with 200 features and want the most accurate fraud score possible.
why: With plenty of labels, a supervised boosted model beats unsupervised anomaly detection.
trap: Anomaly detection is for when you lack labels; here you have millions.

prompt: A sensor dataset has many missing values and skewed features, and you'd rather not spend weeks on preprocessing.
tells: many missing values and skewed features
rather not spend weeks on preprocessing
why: Tree ensembles handle missing values and skew natively.
trap: PCA and linear models need careful scaling and imputation first.

prompt: Predict ad click-through from hundreds of user, ad and context features, where small accuracy gains are worth millions.
tells: hundreds of user, ad and context features
small accuracy gains are worth millions
why: Boosted trees squeeze the most accuracy out of many heterogeneous features.
trap: Logistic regression is a fine baseline, but here accuracy beats interpretability.

prompt: You need both strong accuracy and a ranking of which of 40 tabular features drive the predictions.
tells: ranking of which of 40 tabular features drive
why: Boosted trees plus SHAP values give accuracy and per-feature attributions.
trap: PCA mixes features into components, losing the per-feature story.

prompt: A boosted model scores 0.99 AUC on training data and 0.71 on validation after 5,000 rounds.
tells: 0.99 AUC on training data and 0.71 on validation
why: Classic boosting overfit: use early stopping, a lower learning rate, shallower trees and regularization.
trap: Switching models skips the real lesson: tune boosting's stopping and depth.

prompt: Order search results by predicted relevance using click data and dozens of query and document features.
tells: Order search results by predicted relevance
dozens of query and document features
why: Learning-to-rank with boosted trees (LambdaMART) is a long-standing standard.
trap: Collaborative filtering ignores the query; search ranking depends on it.
